businessType: B2B collaboration/productivity platform (docs, tasks, channels, automation) sold seat-based to enterprises and mid-market. Founded 2017, total raised $90M. Current ARR $12.0M, 45% YoY growth, 300 customers, average 600 licensed seats per enterprise account.
stage: ARR $12.0M, 45% YoY growth. Gross retention 96%. NRR fell from 118% to 104% over a year as seat expansion stalled. Across accounts, active-user adoption (weekly active / licensed seats) fell from 62% to 38% over 18 months as the product added features. Feature count grew 3x in two years; support tickets per seat up 55%; primary ticket themes are 'can't find feature' and 'too complicated.' Cash runway 28 months.
ownerGoal: Lift in-account active adoption back above 60%, restore NRR above 115% via seat expansion, and simplify the product; reach $20M ARR within 15 months to support a Series C.
ownerConstraints: Funding constraint: $90M raised, 28-month runway; Series C is gated on NRR and net-new seat expansion, both of which depend on in-account adoption.

Product constraint: feature count tripled in two years; the UI is cluttered and core workflows are buried. Simplifying the experience (progressive disclosure, role-based defaults, guided core workflows) is a 10-14 week product+design effort; ripping out features risks enterprise contractual dependencies.

Organizational constraint: 130 staff (40 engineering, weighted toward feature delivery; 22 product/design; 24 sales; 20 CS; rest G&A). Product culture has rewarded shipping features over adoption outcomes.
Market constraint: competitors range from simpler point tools to broad suites; the company wins on breadth at purchase but loses daily-use engagement to simpler tools inside the same accounts.

Commercial constraint: expansion revenue depends on growing active seats; when only 38% of licensed seats are active, accounts will not buy more seats, and renewals at flat or reduced seat counts loom.
immediateConcern: In-account adoption has collapsed from 62% to 38% of licensed seats active, NRR has fallen 118%→104% as seat expansion stalls, and support tickets per seat are up 55% with 'too complicated' and 'can't find feature' as top themes, all while the product tripled its feature count. The owner suspects 'product simplicity and expansion' issues and is considering both a simplification effort and new expansion features. But the core pattern is a usability/trust failure inside accounts: licensed users try the product, find it too complex, and abandon it, so trust in daily use erodes and seat expansion is impossible. The owner must decide within the next month whether to keep shipping features (the cultural default), launch a focused simplification/adoption effort, or both, before the Series-C-gating NRR deteriorates further.
